title: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision - Test 3

questions.q: A body of mass $8$ kg~and another of mass $2$ kg are moving with equal kinetic energy. The ratio of their respective momenta will be&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Given: The mass of the objects& ${m}_{1} = 8kg$~and~${m}_{2} = 2kg$.

Let the momentum of the~$8$ kg~and~$2$ kg~masses is~${p}_{1}$~and~${p}_{2}$, respectively, then according to question, their kinetic energy are equal, i.e.,

${K}_{1} = {K}_{2}$

${p}_{1}^{2}2{m}_{1} = {p}_{2}^{2}2{m}_{2}$

$\dfrac{p1}{p2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{m1}{m2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{1}} = \dfrac{2}{1}$

The combined mass collides with $C,$ also perfectly inelastically .~$\dfrac{5}{6}\text{t}\text{h}$ of the initial kinetic energy is lost in the whole process. What is the value of $M / m$?

questions.q: A ball of mass $0 . 15kg$ hits the wall with its initial speed of $12ms^{- 1}$ and bounces back without changing its initial speed. If the force applied by the wall on the ball during the contact is $100N$. calculate the time duration of the contact of ball with the wall.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Given:& $m = 1 . 5kg \text{ and } u = 12ms^{- 1}$

Change in the momentum of the ball after the collision$= 2mv$

$= 2 \times 1 . 5 \times 12$

$= 36Ns$

As the force applied during collision is equal to $100N$ and if $t$~is the duration of collision, so

$100 \times t = \Deltap$

$⇒ t = \dfrac{36}{100}s$

$t = 36 \times {10}^{- 2}s = 0 . 036s$

questions.q: Consider two blocks A and B of masses $m_1=10 \mathrm{~kg}$ and $m_2=5 \mathrm{~kg}$ that are placed on a frictionless table. The block A moves with a constant speed $v=3 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ towards the block B kept at rest. A spring with spring constant $\mathrm{k}=3000 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}$ is attached with the block B as shown in the figure. After the collision, suppose that the blocks A and B, along with the spring in constant compression state, move together, then the compression in the spring is, (Neglect the mass of the spring)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{m}_1 \mathrm{v}_1+\mathrm{m}_2 \mathrm{v}_2=\left(\mathrm{m}_1+\mathrm{m}_2\right) \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{cm}} \\ & \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{cm}} \Rightarrow \frac{10 \times 3}{10+5} \Rightarrow \frac{30}{15}=2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\end{aligned}$
$\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{kx}^2=\frac{1}{2}(10)(3)^2- \left[\frac{1}{2}(15)(2)^2\right]$
$\Rightarrow 90-60=30=3000 x²$
$\begin{aligned} \text{ and } \mathrm{x}^2 \Rightarrow $\frac{30}{3000}=\frac{1}{100}\\ \text{ and } \mathrm{x} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{10} \mathrm{~m}.\end{aligned}$$

questions.q: Two particles of masses $M$ and $2M are$moving with speeds of $10ms^{- 1}$ and $5ms^{- 1}$, as shown in the figure. They collide at the origin and after that they move along the indicated directions with speeds ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$, respectively. The values of ${v}_{1}$~and~ ${v}_{2}$ are, nearly
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
From conservation of linear momentum,
Along $x$-axis:

${10Mcos30}^{0} + 5\left(\text{2M}cos{45}^{0}\right) = \text{M}{v}_{1}cos{30}^{0} + 2\text{M}{v}_{2}cos{45}^{0}$
$10M\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + 10M\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = M\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{v}_{1} + 2M{v}_{2}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
$\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{v}_{1} + \sqrt{2}{v}_{2} = 5 ( \sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2} )$ … (1)
Along $y$-axis:
$- 10M\dfrac{1}{2} + 10M\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = M{v}_{1}\dfrac{1}{2} - 2M{v}_{2}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
$\dfrac{{v}_{1}}{2} - \sqrt{2}{v}_{2} = 5 ( \sqrt{2} - 1 )$ … (2)
From equations (1) and (2)
${v}_{1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 5\left(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\right) + 5 ( \sqrt{2} - 1 )$
${v}_{1} = 13.02m / s$
${v}_{2} = \dfrac{5\sqrt{3} + 5\sqrt{2} - 13.02 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}{\sqrt{2}}$
$= 19.72ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: Three bodies A, B and C have equal kinetic energies and their masses are $400 \mathrm{~g}$. $1.2 \mathrm{~kg}$ and $1.6 \mathrm{~kg}$ respectively. The ratio of their linear momenta is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{KE}=\frac{\mathrm{P}^2}{2 \mathrm{~m}} \\ & \mathrm{P} \propto \sqrt{\mathrm{m}}\end{aligned}$
Hence, $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}: \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}: \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{C}}=\sqrt{400}: \sqrt{1200}: \sqrt{1600}=1: \sqrt{3}: 2$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A& and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A : Body $P$ having mass $M$ moving with speed $u$~has head-on collision elastically with another body $Q$ having mass $m$ initially at rest. If $m ≪ M$, body $Q$ will have a maximum speed equal to $2u$& after collision.

Reason R : During elastic collision, the momentum and kinetic energy are both conserved.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
For $e = 1$ & second body at rest

${V}_{2} = \dfrac{2{m}_{1}{u}_{1}}{{m}_{1} + {m}_{2}} = \dfrac{2u\left(M\right)}{M + m} ≃ 2u$

Since $M > > m$

questions.q: A block of mass $1 . 9kg$ is at rest at the edge of a table, of height 1 m. A bullet of mass $0 . 1kg$ collides with the block and sticks to it. If the velocity of the bullet is $20ms^{- 1}$ in the horizontal direction just before the collision then the kinetic energy just before the combined system strikes the floor, is [Take $g = 10ms^{- 2}$. Assume there is no rotational motion and loss of energy after the collision is negligible.]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Conservation of linear momentum

$0 . 1 \times 20 = \left(0 . 1 + 1 . 9\right) \times v$

$v = 1ms^{- 1}$

Using work energy theorem

${W}_{g} = ∆ k$

$2 \times g \times 1 = k - \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times {1}^{2}$

$∴ k = 21J$

questions.q: Particle& $A$~of mass~${m}_{1}$~moving with velocity~\left(\sqrt{3}\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}\right)\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$~collides with another particle~$B$~of mass~${m}_{2}$~which is at rest initially. Let~$\overset{→}{v}1$~and~$\overset{→}{v}2$~be the velocities of particles~$A$~and~$B$~after collision respectively. If~${m}_{1} = 2{m}_{2}$~and after collision~$\overset{→}{v}1 - \left(\overset{^}{i} + \sqrt{3}\overset{^}{j}\right)\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$, the angle between~$\overset{→}{v}1$~and~$\overset{→}{v}2$ \text{ and } is :$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
${m}_{1}\overset{→}{u}1 + {m}_{2}\overset{→}{u}2 = {m}_{1}\overset{→}{v}1 + {m}_{2}\overset{→}{v}2$

$2{m}_{2} ( \sqrt{3}\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} ) + {m}_{2} \times 0 = 2{m}_{2} ( \overset{^}{i} + \sqrt{3}\overset{^}{j} ) + {m}_{2} \times \overset{→}{v}2$

$2\sqrt{3}\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 2\sqrt{3}\overset{^}{j} + \overset{→}{v}2$

$\overset{→}{v}2 = ( \sqrt{3} - 1 ) \overset{^}{i} - ( \sqrt{3} - 1 ) \overset{^}{j}$

$\overset{→}{v}1 = \overset{^}{i} + \sqrt{3}\overset{^}{j}$

Angle between~$\overset{→}{v}1$~and~$\overset{→}{v}2$~is~${105}^{°}$

& &

questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ moving with velocity $v$~collides with a stationary particle of mass $2m$. After collision, they stick together and continue to move together with velocity
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
The law of conservation of momentum is given as

${m}_{1}u + {m}_{2}u ' = \left({m}_{1} + {m}_{2}\right)v '$

The given data is~

$u = vu ' = 0ms^{- 1}{m}_{1} = m{m}_{2} = 2m$

Using the conservation of momentum equation,

$mv + 2m ( 0 ) = ( m + 2m ) v ' ⇒ v ' = \dfrac{mv}{3m} = \dfrac{v}{3}$

questions.q: An alpha- particle of mass $m$ suffers $1-$ dimensional elastic collision with a nucleus at rest of unknown mass. It is scattered directly backwards losing $64%$ of its initial kinetic energy. The mass of the nucleus is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
From momentum conservation,

$mv + 0 = - m{v}_{1} + M{v}_{2} . . . ( 1 )$~

Using kinetic energy conservation,

$\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}M{v}_{2}^{2} ⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = 0 . 36 \times \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}M{v}_{2}^{2} ⇒ 0 . 64mv^{2} = M{v}_{2}^{2} ⇒ {v}_{2} = 0 . 8v\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{M}}$~

As it retain $36%$,$⇒ 0 . 36 \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2} ⇒ 0 . 36v^{2} = {v}_{1}^{2}$~Hence,~${v}_{1} = 0.6v$
From~$( 1 )$,~$mv = - m \left(0 . 6v\right) + M \left($0 . $8v\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{M}}\right)

$⇒ 1 = - 0 . 6 + 0 . $8\sqrt{\dfrac{M}{m}}

On solving,~we get $M = 4m$

$

questions.q: A body of mass $M$ at rest explodes into three pieces, in the ratio of masses $1: 1: 2$. Two smaller pieces fly off perpendicular to each other with velocities of $30\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ and $40\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ respectively. The velocity of the third piece will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Let the masses of the three parts be& $m ' , m '$~and~$2m '$.

Momentum of first part~${p}_{1} = m ' \times 30 = 30m '$~and momentum of second part~${p}_{2} = m ' \times 40 = 40m '$.

Third part will fly in a direction opposite to the direction of resultant of~${p}_{1}$~and~${p}_{2}$, so that total momentum of the system after explosion remains zero.

Momentum of the third part is~${p}_{3} = \sqrt{{p}_{1}^{2} + {p}_{2}^{2}} = \sqrt{\left(30m '\right)2 + \left(40m '\right)2} = 50m '$

Velocity of third part,~$v = \dfrac{50m '}{2m '} =25ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: As shown below, bob \(A\) of a pendulum having massless string of length ' \(R\) ' is released from \(60^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}\) to the vertical. It hits another bob \(B\) of half the mass that is at rest on a friction less table in the center. Assuming elastic collision, the magnitude of the velocity of bob A after the collision will be (take g as acceleration due to gravity.)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution: Velocity of a just before hitting : $\mathrm{u}=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{~g} \frac{\mathrm{R}}{2}}=\sqrt{\mathrm{gR}}$ Just after collision, let velocity of A and B are $\mathrm{v}_1$ and $v_2$ respectively $\therefore \text { by COM: }\begin{aligned} & m u=m v_1+\frac{m}{2} v_2 \\ & 2 v_1+v_2=2 u ...(i)\\ & e=1=\frac{v_2-v_1}{u} \\ & \Rightarrow v_2-v_1=u..(ii) \end{aligned}$ From (i) -(ii) $\Rightarrow 3 \mathrm{v}_1=\mathrm{u} \Rightarrow \mathrm{v}_1=\frac{\mathrm{u}}{3}=\frac{1}{3} \sqrt{\mathrm{gR}}$

questions.q: Consider a uniform rod of mass $M = 4m$ and length $l$ pivoted about its centre. A mass $m$ moving with velocity $v$ making angle $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ to the rod’s long axis collides with one end of the rod and sticks to it. The angular speed of the rod-mass system just after the collision is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
${L}_{oi} = {L}_{of}$
$\dfrac{mV}{\sqrt{2}} \times \dfrac{L}{2} = \left[\dfrac{4mL^{2}}{12} + \dfrac{mL^{2}}{4}\right] \times \omega$
$\omega = \dfrac{6V}{7\sqrt{2}L} = \dfrac{3\sqrt{2}V}{7L}$

questions.q: As per the given figure, a small ball $P$~slides down the quadrant of a circle and hits the other ball $Q$ of equal mass which is initially at rest. Neglecting the effect of friction and assume the collision to be elastic, the velocity of ball $Q$ after collision will be : $( g = 10ms^{- 2} )$&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Let& ${v}_{p}$~be the velocity of ball~$P$~just before collision. Therefore, applying conservation of energy for~$P$~(between the moment it is released and~the moment just before collision),

$mgl + 0 = \dfrac{1}{2}m{vp}^{2}$

$⇒ {v}_{p} = \sqrt{2gl}$

~ ~ ~ ~ $= \sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 0 . 2}$

~ ~ ~ ~ ~$= 2ms^{- 1}$~

Since both balls have equal masses and the collision~is perfectly elastic, the velocities of both the balls will get interchanged.

Therefore, the velocity of ball $Q$~just after the collision is~$2ms^{- 1}$.

questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ is moving with speed $2\text{v}$ and collides with a mass $2m$ moving with speed $\text{v}$ in the same direction. After the collision, the first mass is stopped completely while the second one splits into two particles each of mass $m,$ which move at an angle ${45}^{o}$ with respect to the original direction. The speed of each of the moving particle will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
$

As $2m$ splits into equal parts, ${v}_{1} = {v}_{2}$ and $\theta = 4{5}^{0}$
From conservation of linear momentum,
$m \left(2v\right) + 2m \left($v\right) = 2 \left[m{v}_{1}cos ⁡ 4{5}^{o}\right]$
$⇒ {v}_{1} = {v}_{2} = 2\sqrt{2}\text{v}$

questions.q: A body of mass $M$~moving at speed ${V}_{0}$ collides elastically with a mass $m$~at rest. After the collision, the two masses move at angles ${θ}_{1}$ and ${θ}_{2}$ with respect to the initial direction of motion of the body of mass $M .$. The largest possible value of the ratio $\dfrac{M}{m},$~for which the angles ${θ}_{1}$ and ${θ}_{2}$ will be equal, is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Linear momentum conservation
(i) $y$-direction
$m{v}_{2}sin\theta = m{v}_{1}sin\theta$
$m{v}_{2} = m{v}_{1}$~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~...(1)
(ii) $x$-direction
$m{v}_{0} = m{v}_{2}cos\theta + m{v}_{1}cos\theta$~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ...(2)
from (1) and (2)
$m{v}_{0} = m{v}_{2}cos\theta + m{v}_{2}cos\theta$
$m{v}_{0} = 2m{v}_{2}cos\theta$~ ~ ~ ~...(3)
(iii) $e = 1$given
$\dfrac{{v}_{2} - {v}_{1}cos2\theta}{{v}_{0}cos\theta} = 1$
${v}_{2} - {v}_{1}cos2\theta = {v}_{0}cos\theta$~ ~ ~ ~...(4)
${v}_{2} - \dfrac{{m}_{2}2}{M}cos2\theta = {v}_{0}cos\theta$
${v}_{2}\left[1 - \dfrac{m}{M}cos2\theta\right] = {v}_{0}cos\theta$
$\dfrac{m{v}_{0}}{2mcos\theta}\left[1 - \dfrac{m}{M}cos2\theta\right] = {v}_{0}cos\theta$
$M - mcos2\theta = 2mcos2\theta$
$M = 2m\cos^{2}\theta + m \lleft(2\cos^{2}\theta -1\right)$
$\dfrac{M}{m} ==4\cos^{2}\theta -$1$
\left(\dfrac{M}{m}\right)max = 4 - 1 = 3$

questions.q: A body of mass $1 \mathrm{~kg}$ falls freely from a height of $100 \mathrm{~m}$, on a platform of mass $3 \mathrm{~kg}$ which is mounted on a spring having spring constant $\mathrm{k}=1.25 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}$. The bodysticks to the platform and the spring's maximum compression is found to be $x$. Given that $g=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2},$ the value of $\mathrm{x}$ will be close to :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution: Velocity of $1 \mathrm{~kg}$ block just before it collides with $3 \mathrm{~kg}$ block $=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{gh}}=\sqrt{2000} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ Using principle of conservation of linear momentum just before and just after collision, we get $1 \times \sqrt{2000}=4 \mathrm{v} \Rightarrow \mathrm{v}=\frac{\sqrt{2000}}{4} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ Initial compression of spring $1.25 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{x}_{0}=30 \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}_{0} \approx 0$ using work energy theorem, $\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{g}}+\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{sp}}=\Delta \mathrm{KE}\Rightarrow 40 \times x+\frac{1}{2} \times 1.25 \times 10^{6}\left(0^{2}-x^{2}\right)=0-\frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times v^{2}$ solving $x \approx 4 \mathrm{~cm}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A) :
Three identical spheres of same mass undergo one dimensional motion as shown in figure with initial velocities $v_{\mathrm{A}}=5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}, v_{\mathrm{B}}=2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}, v_{\mathrm{C}}=4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. If we wait sufficiently long for elastic collision to happen, then $v_{\mathrm{A}}=4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}, v_{\mathrm{B}}=2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$, $v_{\mathrm{C}}=5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ will be the final velocities. Reason (R): In an elastic collision between identical masses, two objects exchange their velocities. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.q: A bullet of $10g$, moving with velocity $v$, collides head-on with the stationary bob of a pendulum and recoils with velocity $100ms^{- 1}$. The length of the pendulum is $0 . 5m$ and mass of the bob is $1$ kg. The minimum value of $v\text{in}ms^{- 1}$, so that the pendulum describes a circle. (Assume the string to be inextensible and $g = 10ms^{- 2}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Final velocity of system (bullet $+$ mass) should be $= \sqrt{5gr}$

Now $M\sqrt{5gr} = m ( v + 100 )$

thus $v = \dfrac{M}{m}\sqrt{5gr} - 100 = 500 - 100 = 400ms^{- 1}$

$v = 400ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: The distance of centre of mass from end $A$ of a one dimensional rod  \left(AB\right)$ having mass density $ρ = {ρ}_{0}\left(1 - \dfrac{x2}{L2}\right)kgm^{- 1}$ and length $L$ (in meter) is $\dfrac{3L}{α}m$. The value of $\alpha$ is _____ (where $x$ is the distance form end $A$)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Given here:

Mass density,& $ρ = {ρ}_{0}\left(1 - \dfrac{x2}{L2}\right)kgm^{- 1}$

Let us suppose there is an element of length~$d x$~at a distance $x$ from left must end.

Mass of this element is~$d m = ρ d x = {ρ}_{0} \left($1 - $\dfrac{x2}{L2}\right)

The centre of mass of this element is~${X}_{cm} = $\dfrac{∫ xdm}{∫ dm}

$= $\dfrac{{ρ}_{0}{∫}_{0}^{l}\left(x - \dfrac{x2}{L2}\right)x d x}{{∫}_{0}^{l}{ρ}_{0}\left(1 - \dfrac{x2}{L2}\right) d x}

$= $\dfrac{\dfrac{L2}{2} - \dfrac{L4}{4L^{2}}}{L - \dfrac{L3}{3L^{2}}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{L2}{4}}{\dfrac{2L}{3}} = \dfrac{3L}{8}

Hence, the value of~\alpha =$8$.

$

questions.q: A particle of mass& $m$ is moving along the $x$-axis with initial velocity $u\overset{^}{i}$. It collides elastically with a particle of mass~$10m$ at rest and then moves with half its initial kinetic energy (see figure). If $sin{θ}_{1} = \sqrt{n}sin{θ}_{2}$& then value of n is ________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
From momentum conservation in perpendicular direction of initial motion.
${mv}_{1}{sinθ}_{1} = 10{mv}_{2}{sinθ}_{2}$
Given that \left(\dfrac{1}{2}{mu}^{2}\right)\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}{mv}_{1}^{2} \ldots \ldots . ( 2 )$
From equation (1) & (2)
${sinθ}_{1} = \sqrt{10}{sinθ}_{2}$
$n = 10

questions.q: The identical spheres each of mass $2M$ are placed at the corners of a right angled triangle with mutually perpendicular sides equal to $4m$ each. Taking point of intersection of these two sides as origin, the magnitude of position vector of the centre of mass of the system is $\dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{x}$, where the value of $x$ is ________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Position vector $\overset{→}{r}COM = \dfrac{{m}_{1}\overset{→}{r}1 + {m}_{2}\overset{→}{r}2 + {m}_{3}\overset{→}{r}3}{{m}_{1} + {m}_{2} + {m}_{3}}$

$\overset{→}{r}\text{COM} = \dfrac{2M \times 0 + 2M \times 4\overset{^}{i} + 2M \times 4\overset{^}{j}}{6M}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{r} = \dfrac{4}{3}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{4}{3}\overset{^}{j}$

$| \overset{→}{r} | = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)2 + \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)2} = \dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{3}$

Therefore, $x = 3$.

questions.q: The momentum of a body is increased by $50 %$. The percentage increase in the kinetic energy of the body is________ % .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
The relation of kinetic energy and momentum is given by

$K = \dfrac{p2}{2m}$

The new value of momentum is~$p ' = 1 . 5p$

The new value of kinetic energy is

$⇒ K ' = \dfrac{\left(1 . 5p\right)2}{2m} = 2 . 25K$

Hence, the percentage increase in kinetic energy is~

$\dfrac{K ' - K}{K} \times 100 = \dfrac{2 . 25K - K}{K} = 125 %$
